{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
I bombed my interview at my dream company so badly that I cried in the parking lot. That humiliation made me completely rethink my approach. I spent a year building skills I'd ignored. When I reapplied, I didn't just get the job—I got a role two levels higher than I'd originally sought.

CANDIDATE A:
My first restaurant failed within eight months. Bankrupt and ashamed, I took a job washing dishes. Watching that kitchen taught me everything my business school hadn't. My second restaurant, built on those lessons, now has two Michelin stars.

CANDIDATE B:
I prepared extensively for my interview at my dream company. It went well—I answered every question confidently and connected with the hiring manager. They offered me the position a week later. Hard work led to success along the path I'd planned.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:14"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both the SITUATION and CANDIDATE A involve initial failure leading to a period of reflection and skill-building, resulting in a greater success than originally sought."}
